nodes.title: The Witt frame
nodes.statement: For a ring R in which p is nilpotent, or a p-adically complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion, the Witt frame is 𝒲_R = (W(R), I_R = V(W(R)) = ker(W(R) → R), F, F₁ = V^{-1}, p): F is the Witt Frobenius and F₁ : I_R → W(R) the inverse of the injective Verschiebung onto I_R, so F = p·F₁ on I_R. It is a frame in Lau's sense (I_R + pW(R) lies in the radical of W(R)); its formation is functorial in R and defines a frame of sheaves W(𝒪) on the p-completely faithfully flat site of R.
hypotheses: Frames in Lau's generality (node PD.0/frame with completeness replaced by I_R + pW(R) ⊆ Rad W(R)).
proofSteps: V is injective with image I_R; F(V(x)) = p·x gives F = pF₁ on I_R (Mathlib WittVector.frobenius and WittVector.verschiebung, with WittVector.frobenius_verschiebung).
I_R + pW(R) lies in the radical since R is p-adically complete (Zink 2002, §1; Lau 2010, §2, the Witt frame example).
acceptance: For k perfect, 𝒲_k = (W(k), pW(k), F, F/p, p).
For R = F_p[ε]/ε², I_R contains V([ε]) with F₁(V[ε]) = [ε].

nodes.title: Displays
nodes.statement: Let R be p-complete. A display over R is a window over the Witt frame of sheaves W(𝒪) on the p-completely faithfully flat site of R; equivalently (by descent) a window (P, Q, F, F₁) over 𝒲_R: P a finite projective W(R)-module, I_R P ⊆ Q ⊆ P with P/Q finite projective over R, F and F₁ = V^{-1} semilinear with the window axioms. Disp(R) is the category of displays. A display is F-nilpotent if its Frobenius is nilpotent modulo p. For R of characteristic p these are Zink's displays of PELModuli M2.15 (3n-displays) and F-nilpotence is Zink's nilpotence condition.
hypotheses: p-complete R with bounded p^∞-torsion for the descent statement.
proofSteps: Window over 𝒲 (node witt-frame, node PD.0/window).

Displays satisfy faithfully flat descent (Zink 2002, Theorem 37), and over p-complete rings with bounded p^∞-torsion are compatible systems of displays over R/p^n, so the sheaf-theoretic definition agrees with windows over 𝒲_R (Anschütz–Le Bras, Definition 5.3.1 and Remark 5.3.2, pp. 87–88).
acceptance: In the contravariant normalisation of the source, Z_k(μ_{p^∞}) = (W(k), Fil = W(k), F = pσ) is F-nilpotent and Z_k(ℚ_p/ℤ_p) = (W(k), Fil = pW(k), F = σ) is not (node display-functor).

nodes.title: The Nygaard frame maps to the Witt frame
nodes.statement: Let R be quasi-regular semiperfectoid with pR = 0 or R p-torsion-free. The projection Δ_R → Δ_R/N^{≥1}Δ_R ≅ R lifts to a u-morphism of frames f : Δ_{R,Nyg} → 𝒲_R, where u ∈ W(R)^× satisfies p = u·f(ξ̃).
hypotheses: As stated; ξ̃ generates I.
proofSteps: By the adjunction between δ-rings and Witt vectors (Joyal), Δ_R → R lifts to a δ-ring map f : Δ_R → W(R) sending N^{≥1}Δ_R into I_R; f(ξ) ∈ I_R, so f(ξ̃) = F(f(ξ)) = p·F₁(f(ξ)), and F₁(f(ξ)) is a unit u^{-1} (checked modulo the radical); the divided Frobenii match up to u (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 5.3.3, p. 88).
acceptance: R = k perfect: Δ_k = W(k) and f is the identity with u = 1.
R perfectoid p-torsion-free: f : A_inf(R) → W(R) is induced by θ.

nodes.title: The display of a p-divisible group
nodes.statement: Let R be quasi-syntomic. For G ∈ BT(R) put Z_R(G) = ℳ_Δ(G) ⊗_{O^pris} W(𝒪) with Frobenius φ ⊗ F, and Fil Z_R(G) generated by I(𝒪)·Z_R(G) and the image of φ^{-1}(I^pris·ℳ_Δ(G)). There is a unique way to complete this to a functor Z_R : BT(R) → Disp(R), natural in R, which for R quasi-regular semiperfectoid with pR = 0 or R p-torsion-free is the composite of ℳ_Δ (as windows over the Nygaard frame, node PD.1/nygaard-windows) with base change along the frame map of node nygaard-to-witt-frame. For p = 2 the functor is not an antiequivalence on all p-divisible groups.
hypotheses: R quasi-syntomic.
proofSteps: Only F₁ has to be constructed. For R p-torsion-free quasi-regular semiperfectoid it is the window base change, unique since W(R) is p-torsion-free; descend to p-torsion-free quasi-syntomic R (displays form a stack, node display).
For general R, write R locally as a quotient of a p-torsion-free quasi-syntomic ring and use the uniqueness and naturality (Anschütz–Le Bras, Proposition 5.3.4 and its proof, pp. 88–89).
acceptance: For R = k perfect, Z_k(G) is the classical display of G (Dieudonné module with V^{-1} on Q).
For G = μ_{p^∞}, Fil Z_R(G) = Z_R(G) because Fil ℳ_Δ(μ_{p^∞}) = ℳ_Δ(μ_{p^∞}); for G = ℚ_p/ℤ_p, Fil Z_R(G) = I(𝒪)·Z_R(G) + image of N^{≥1}O^pris.

nodes.title: Formal p-divisible groups are F-nilpotent displays (Zink, Lau)
nodes.statement: Let R be quasi-syntomic and flat over ℤ/p^n for some n > 0 or over ℤ_p. The functor Z_R restricts to an antiequivalence BT_f(R) ≃ Disp_nilp(R) between formal p-divisible groups over R and F-nilpotent displays over R.
hypotheses: Formal: G is a p-divisible formal Lie group, i.e. G = colim G[p^n] is connected (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1/serre-tate-connected-p-divisible).

The proof printed by Anschütz–Le Bras (via topological nilpotence of the divided Frobenius on ker(A_crys(R) → W(R))) is retracted by their 2025 erratum: that nilpotence fails (Senger's example, source issue AL23 E5 of the paper extraction). The statement is planned from Zink's and Lau's proofs.
proofSteps: Zink constructs a functor BT from F-nilpotent displays to formal p-divisible groups for every ring R in which p is nilpotent (and by limits p-adic R), and proves it is an equivalence for R excellent local or with R/pR of finite type over a field (Zink 2002, Theorems 9 and 103).

Lau proves that BT is an equivalence for every R in which p is nilpotent (Lau 2008, Theorem 1.1), by deformation theory: Grothendieck–Messing for both sides along PD thickenings (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4/grothendieck-messing) and the case of perfect fields.

Compatibility: on quasi-syntomic R as stated, Z_R is quasi-inverse to BT, since both are compatible with base change and agree on the crystalline Dieudonné modules (node PD.4/crystalline-comparison) of the special fibres and on Hodge filtrations; uniqueness of the functor in node display-functor identifies them.

nodes.title: Étale comparison for the prismatic Dieudonné crystal
nodes.statement: Let R be quasi-syntomic, α : Spa(R[1/p], R)^♦_v → (R)_{qsyn,qrsp} and j the open complement of V(I) (generic fibre) as in the source. (1) α_*(ℤ/p^n) ≅ (O^pris/p^n)^{φ = 1} and (α ∘ j)_*(ℤ/p^n) ≅ (O^pris/p^n[1/I])^{φ = 1} (non-derived invariants). (2) For a p-divisible group G over R and n ≥ 0, j^*α^*((ℳ_Δ(G)/p^n)[1/I]^{φ = 1}) ≅ Hom_{ℤ/p^n}(G[p^n]_η, ℤ/p^n), where G[p^n]_η is the sheaf Spa(S[1/p], S) ↦ G[p^n](S[1/p]); and (α ∘ j)^*G[p^n] ≅ G[p^n]_η.

(2): ℳ_Δ(G)/p^n = ℋom(G[p^n], O^pris/p^n) (node PD.2/tate-module-description and the proof of node PD.4/pdiv-locally-free); invert I, take φ-fixed points with (1), and use Lemma 5.4.3 to identify the pullback of G[p^n] (Proposition 5.4.2 and Lemma 5.4.3, pp. 92–93).
